Thought: I need to evaluate each statement and determine which one is incorrect.

A. Enamines are formed between secondary amines and the carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones.
This is correct. Enamines are formed when secondary amines react with aldehydes or ketones. The reaction involves nucleophilic addition of the amine to the carbonyl group, followed by dehydration.

B. Hydrolysis of an acetal is catalyzed by acids.
This is correct. Acetals are hydrolyzed under acidic conditions. The acid protonates one of the oxygen atoms, making it a better leaving group, which facilitates the hydrolysis reaction.

C. Hydrolysis of an acetal is catalyzed by bases.
This statement is suspicious. Acetals are typically stable under basic conditions and are hydrolyzed under acidic conditions, not basic conditions. This appears to be incorrect.

D. Oximes are stabilized by conjugation between the C=N and OH groups.
This is correct. Oximes (R₂C=N-OH) have conjugation between the C=N double bond and the lone pairs on the oxygen of the OH group, which provides stabilization.

Based on my analysis, statement C appears to be incorrect because acetals are hydrolyzed under acidic conditions, not basic conditions.
